# PDF parsing regression fixtures

Deterministic, dependency-free PDF fixtures for the PDF-parsing test suite.

Everything here is generated by [`make_fixtures.py`](make_fixtures.py), a
pure-standard-library script that writes valid PDFs by hand (objects, an xref
table with real byte offsets, a trailer with `/Root`, and `startxref`). No
third-party package is needed to build them, and no font is embedded.

## Regenerating

```sh
python3 tests/fixtures/make_fixtures.py
```

This rewrites every file in [`pdf/`](pdf/) and [`manifest.json`](manifest.json).
The generator uses no timestamps, no randomness and no compression, so it is
**deterministic and idempotent**: running it twice produces byte-identical
files (verified with `shasum -a 256`).

The PDFs are committed as binaries. Regenerate only when a fixture definition
changes, and commit the new binaries and manifest together.

## Conventions

* Standard-14 fonts only: `F1` Helvetica, `F2` Helvetica-Bold, `F3`
  Times-Roman, `F4` Times-Italic, all with `/Encoding /WinAnsiEncoding`.
* All text is plain ASCII (no smart quotes, no Unicode), so `pdftotext`
  extracts it exactly. The only non-ASCII bytes in the files are the standard
  binary file-header marker and the raw image pixel data.
* One `BT ... Tj ET` block per physical line for precise positioning.
* Units are points. All geometry in the manifest is PDF user space with the
  origin at the bottom-left of the **unrotated** MediaBox. Annotation
  `/Rect` and `/QuadPoints` values are recorded exactly as stored in the PDF,
  even on pages that carry `/Rotate`.
* A `paragraph` is one logical block; `paragraphs[].lines` lists its physical
  lines with the page each was drawn on, so paragraphs split across a page
  break have `pages: [1, 2]`.
* `annotations[].covers` is the exact body text enclosed by the annotation
  rect (verified against word boxes); it is `null` for margin sticky notes and
  the Square, whose `refers_to` field names the nearby anchor paragraph
  instead.
* `running_elements` lists running headers, footers and standalone page
  numbers that a body-text parser must discard.

## Fixtures

| File | Pages | What it contains | Bug class it guards |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `simple.pdf` | 1 A4 | Helvetica-Bold 16 title plus three short plain paragraphs, no numbering. | Baseline extraction, paragraph joining and attribution. |
| `paragraphs.pdf` | 1 A4 | Heading, numbered paragraphs `1.`/`2.`/`3.` with several lines each, and an `(a)`/`(b)` sub-list under paragraph 3. | Numbered-paragraph detection, hanging-indent joining, sub-list vs paragraph confusion. |
| `paragraphs_paged.pdf` | 2 A4 | Paragraph 2 starts at the bottom of page 1 and continues at the top of page 2, with the running header `Article 9 (continued)` in between. | Cross-page paragraph continuation: a naive parser injects the header into the paragraph and splits it. |
| `twocolumn.pdf` | 1 A4 | Full-width title, left column x=50..280 and right column x=315..545. The content stream emits **all** left lines before any right line, but the two columns' y positions interleave. Sentences start with `LEFT`/`RIGHT`. | Column detection: sorting lines by y alone interleaves the columns into nonsense. |
| `fontsizes.pdf` | 1 A4 | 20pt Helvetica-Bold title, 14pt Helvetica-Bold section heading, 11pt body, a Times-Italic run and a 9pt footnote. | Font/size recovery, heading-vs-body-vs-footnote classification, italic runs. |
| `image.pdf` | 2 A4 | Page 1: a paragraph plus an 8x8 RGB image XObject scaled into the middle third. Page 2: an image over almost the whole page and **no text**. | Image XObject discovery and image-only/"scanned" pages (page 2 must yield no text). |
| `vector.pdf` | 1 A4 | Stroked and filled rectangles, connecting `m`/`l`/`S` lines, a filled `f` path, and a caption below. | Vector-graphics detection distinct from text and images; caption placement. |
| `rotated.pdf` | 2 A4 | Page 1 `/Rotate 90`, page 2 `/Rotate 270`; two text lines each drawn to read left-to-right after rotation; page 1 also has a Highlight. Unrotated `/MediaBox`. | Rotated-page text order and mapping between stored (unrotated) annotation rects and displayed space. |
| `pagesizes.pdf` | 3 | A4 portrait (595.276x841.89), US Letter (612x792), real A4 landscape (841.89x595.276, `/Rotate 0`). | Page-size handling; landscape detected from the MediaBox, not from `/Rotate`. |
| `headers.pdf` | 4 A4 | Running header `International Law Review`, running footer `Page N of 4`, and one body paragraph that flows continuously across all four page breaks (pages 2-4 start mid-sentence). Page 2 also has a standalone centred `- 2 -` page-number line. | Header/footer stripping and continuous body flow across page breaks. |
| `empty.pdf` | 2 A4 | Completely empty content streams. | Blank pages: no crash, two pages, no text. |
| `minimal.pdf` | 1 A4 | A single `.` glyph, 12pt Helvetica, nothing else. | Degenerate-but-valid input treated as (almost) no text, not an error. |
| `annotated.pdf` | 2 A4 | Six numbered paragraphs carrying all five annotation subtypes. Page 1: Highlight over the middle line of paragraph 2, a Text sticky note in the right margin beside paragraph 3, an Underline over paragraph 4, a Square in the margin — stored in the `/Annots` array deliberately **out of vertical order**. Page 2: a StrikeOut over paragraph 5 and a Highlight plus Text note whose rects overlap. | Annotation parsing (`/Subtype`, `/Rect`, `/QuadPoints`, `/Contents`, `/T`, `/C`), rect-to-text mapping, overlapping annotations, and input-order vs sorted-order of `/Annots`. |

## Manifest

`manifest.json` has `format: "ila-pdf-fixtures/1"` and a `field_notes` section
describing every field. Each fixture entry carries the file name, description,
guarded bug class, page count, byte length, `sha256`, and per-page
width/height/rotation plus the expected headings, paragraphs, images, vector
elements, annotations and running elements.

## Verification performed

```sh
# page count, per-page size and rotation
pdfinfo -f 1 -l <n> pdf/<file>.pdf

# text extraction (per page and whole document)
pdftotext pdf/<file>.pdf -
pdftotext -f <n> -l <n> pdf/<file>.pdf -

# annotations, images, drawings (throwaway venv, not a project dependency)
/tmp/ilaprobe/bin/python -c "import pymupdf; ..."
```

Observed results (poppler 26.09.0, PyMuPDF 1.28.2):

* `pdfinfo` reports the expected page count and, per page, exactly the
  manifest MediaBox and `/Rotate` for all 13 files — including
  `pagesizes.pdf` (A4 / Letter / landscape-A4) and `rotated.pdf` (90 and 270).
* `pdftotext` extracts every expected line verbatim for all fixtures. It
  reports 0 characters for `empty.pdf` and 1 character (`.`) for
  `minimal.pdf`.
* PyMuPDF sees the expected annotation counts and subtypes
  (`annotated.pdf`: 4 on page 1, 3 on page 2; `rotated.pdf`: 1 Highlight) with
  the expected `/T` authors and `/Contents`. Every non-null `covers` value is
  a superset of the word boxes falling inside the annotation rect.
* The overlapping Highlight and Text note on `annotated.pdf` page 2 intersect
  (175.1 square points); the raw `/Annots` order on page 1 is
  `Square, Underline, Highlight, Text`, which is not sorted by y.
* `image.pdf` reports one image per page at the expected bounding boxes;
  `vector.pdf` reports 7 vector drawings matching the manifest.

### Known caveat: `twocolumn.pdf` and `pdftotext`

The fixture is specified so that the *content stream* emits the left column
before the right column while the lines' y positions interleave. Sorting those
lines by y alone produces the expected interleaved nonsense:

```
LEFT alpha begins the first left
RIGHT alpha begins the first right
column paragraph and continues.
column paragraph and continues.
...
```

Poppler's default `pdftotext` output, however, applies its own column analysis
and already reconstructs the correct reading order (left column fully, then
right column); `pdftotext -raw` also emits the correct order because the stream
order is left-then-right. So this fixture cannot fail against this poppler
version — it is a real regression test for parsers that order lines by y only,
not for `pdftotext`. This is a property of the specified fixture, not a defect
in the generated file.

### Minor extraction normalization

`pdftotext` renders the standalone `- 2 -` line of `headers.pdf` as `-2-`
(it collapses the spaces around the hyphen). The content stream and the
manifest contain the literal string `- 2 -`.

### `hiddentext.pdf`
One A4 page whose text is drawn with the invisible text rendering mode
(`3 Tr`) over a full-page image -- i.e. an OCR layer on a scanned page.
Guards the `pdftohtml -hidden` path: without it a fully searchable scanned
judgment extracts as a document with no text at all, and the tool reports
"no text layer" for a PDF that plainly has one.
